newsitem.title: USA: Phillips Q3 E&P up 98 pct on flat production.
newsitem.headline: Phillips Q3 E&P up 98 pct on flat production.

text.p: Phillips Petroleum Co said the 38 percent net income gain in third quarter of 1996 over the last year's third quarter was due mainly to substantially improved earnings from the exploration and production (E&P) and natural gas operations.
Phillips said its average worldwide crude price for the period was $4.90 a barrel higher at $20.54, while average U.S. natural gas was up 63 cents per thousand cubic feet at $1.91.
E&P net operating income was up 98 percent from the year-earlier period, even with worldwide crude production about the same and natural gas production up just four percent.

Net operating income from refining and marketing was down in third quarter 1996 at $33 million, compared with $36 million in third quarter 1995. Phillips said this was due mainly to lower motor fuel margins, though higher distillates margins and volumes helped alleviate that.

Philips average sales prices for gasoline were up 15.5 percent and 10.8 percent at 67 cents a gallon and 82 cents a gallon respectively for wholesale and retail, while distillate prices were 21 percent up at 63 cents a gallon. Those prices trailed well behind the 32.5 percent gain in the average crude oil price realized by Phillips in third quarter 1996 against the third quarter 1995.
